fact: Biometric Update, citing Tech Review Africa, reports that Mozambique's Digital Certification System operates under the country's Electronic Transactions Law and Digital Certification Regulation; the report gives no enactment date, so it is dated to the document's published date.

The report names a Digital Certification Regulation under which, with the Electronic Transactions Law, the Digital Certification System operates and which is meant to establish the authenticity and integrity of digital signatures; it gives no date for the regulation, so it is dated to the published date.

Decree No. 40/2026 of the Council of Ministers, on Simple Prior Notification for economic activities, gives the electronic signature the same legal standing as a handwritten one, as reported by Lusa via 360 Mozambique; the regime takes effect within 90 days and the decree's own date is not given, so this is dated to the published date.

fact: DLA Piper's guide, last modified 17 February 2026, lists the Electronic Transactions Law (Law no. 3/2017 of 9 January) among Mozambique's laws in force and cites its rules on electronic marketing consent, intermediary service providers and personal data, with fines for breach.

DLA Piper's guide, last modified 17 February 2026, says Decree no. 59/2023 of 27 October (amended by Decree no. 44/2025 of 28 November) requires intermediary electronic service providers, a category the Electronic Transactions Law defines, and digital platform operators to register and be licensed with INTIC.

The UNECA/GIZ/AU inception report for INTIC, dated 19 June 2025, cites the Electronic Transactions Law (Law no. 03/2017 of 9 January 2017) as an existing Mozambican law with provisions on e-commerce, electronic transactions and personal data.
TechAfrica News reports Mozambique's Electronic Transactions Law is being implemented, with the first licences to digital operators issued under it on 2026-06-08.

The report says the Electronic Transactions Law has supporting regulations that set up registration, supervision and licensing of intermediate electronic service providers and digital platform operators; no regulation is dated.

INTIC's board president said 19 licences had been issued to intermediate electronic service providers and digital platform operators out of about 170 registered companies under evaluation, at a ceremony in Maputo on 2026-06-08.
A law journal article by Bitone Viage lists the Lei das Transações Eletrónicas among the relevant legal instruments existing in Mozambique.
UNESCO's profile names the Electronic Transactions Law (2017) as an existing regulatory instrument in Mozambique.
The statement says Mozambique approved the Electronic Transactions Law in 2017 (Law No. 3/2017, of 9 January), setting the legal framework for electronic commerce and digital signatures.
INTIC says the digital certification work implements Law 3/2017 of 9 January, the Electronic Transactions Law.
INTIC says Decree 59/2019 of 3 July, the Regulation of the Digital Certification System, is the instrument made for the system under the Electronic Transactions Law.
INTIC says Law no. 3/2017 and Decree no. 59/2019 give digital signatures the same legal validity as physical ones.

INTIC reports that Rosa Dique named the Lei das Transaccoes Electronicas among Mozambique's existing legal bases, with the Constitution, the Labour Law and the Malabo Convention, for protecting privacy and personal data.
INTIC cites Lei n.o 3/2017 of 9 January, the Lei de Transacções Electrónicas, as setting obligations for processing personal data electronically.
